subject: Science
stem: A simple pendulum (a small bob suspended from a string) swings back and forth at regular intervals. The time taken to complete one full swing (there and back) is called its:
explanation: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation — amplitude is the maximum displacement from the resting position, and frequency (the reciprocal of time period) is the number of oscillations per second.

subject: Science
stem: Isaac Newton's principle stating that every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, is known as the:
explanation: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation explains why objects fall toward Earth and why planets orbit the Sun — it applies to ALL masses in the universe, distinct from Newton's Laws of Motion (which describe how forces affect an object's movement, not the specific gravitational attraction between masses).

subject: Science
stem: When a ball is dropped from a height (ignoring air resistance), it speeds up continuously as it falls due to Earth's gravitational pull. The rate at which its speed increases every second is called the:
explanation: Acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth) is the constant rate at which a freely falling object speeds up — distinct from terminal velocity (the maximum constant speed reached when air resistance balances gravity) or escape velocity (the minimum speed needed to break free of a planet's gravity entirely).
